page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-32 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 124 GB of RAM. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor, the server provides 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor architecture includes a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core CPU execution, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core metrics placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is also highly competitive, with Geekbench multi-core scores reaching the top tier, while stress-ng multi-core benchmarks fall into the average range. Memory performance is strong, as evidenced by a high PassMark memory score and uncached read bandwidth of 103.22 GB/sec. The system excels in single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, achieving top-tier results in gzip and bzip3 benchmarks. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong static web serving throughput and top-tier text generation speeds for small language models, though medium-sized model inference remains in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4d-standard-32 offers a balanced resource density of approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, making it a viable option for workloads requiring dedicated compute resources without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Given its strong single-core performance, robust cryptographic capabilities, and balanced memory-to-CPU ratio, this instance is well-suited for web serving, text and image processing, software compilation, and small-scale language model inference.
